text:
Anya: Heads-up: a customer (zenith-ai) flagged invoice_preview showing ~30% higher tokens than their final invoice for March 28. Preview = 13.1k tokens, final = 10.0k.

Omar: That's pretty big. Do we have a sample event_id?

Anya: yes event_id=evt-20260328-9921. Pasted the edge envelope: 
```json
{"event_id":"evt-20260328-9921","req_id":"r-9921","tenant":"zenith-ai","model_requested":"gpt4x","model_route":"canary-preview","model_served":"gpt4x-compact-quant","tokens_in":300,"tokens_out":1200}
```

Becky: Quick Q: preview pipeline uses aggregated partials by (sampling_id, model_alias) right? Final billing replays raw events and applies req_id dedupe.

Clarence: Correct. We've seen preview inflation when fallback paths split aggregates across model_alias variants or when route attributes are mutated mid-flight.

Anya: I did a join: preview.aggregates vs billing.raw_events for that window. Found 2 partial aggregates for r-9921: one with model_alias_raw='gpt4x-compact-quant' tokens=150 and another with model_alias_after_normalize='gpt4x-compact' tokens=1350 -> preview sums both -> 1500. Final dedupe by req_id -> 1500 (but tokenization factor later normalized gave 1200?). Hmm need to spell out where 30% comes from.

Omar: Maybe token factor mapping differs between preview and final. Can you show the tokenization factor applied?

Anya: Preview used factor 1.0 for alias 'gpt4x-compact-quant'. Billing map normalized alias to 'gpt4x-compact' with factor 0.8, so final tokens=1.0*1500*0.8=1200 -> that's lower. But original final invoice shows 1000 not 1200. Another layer: we have a per-tenant discount multiplier applied after invoice generation for reserved capacity. That might have reduced to 1000. So delta chain: preview (no reservation discount *before normalization) vs final (normalized alias + reservation discount).

Becky: So multiple transformations at different stages: alias normalization, tokenization factor, reservation discount. We should standardize ordering: tokenization should use canonical alias and reservation discount applied at the invoice display layer, not in token counting.

Clarence: Agreed. Short-term mitigation options: A) make preview pipeline read from the normalized alias topic, B) expand sku_map to accept alias synonyms and normalize factors in preview, C) add a preview computation footnote with expected discount and normalization differences.

Omar: Which is least risky?

Becky: B is quick. Update sku_map by adding synonyms mapping raw->canonical with same token_factor as final. That will align preview token counts with final before discount. Then show discount separately in console.

deploy-bot: router-normalizer v4.0.1 was deployed 2026-03-27T20:03Z. Change: canonicalize model_alias and emit header X-Canonical-Model.

Anya: Good to know. That explains why consumer pipelines are split on whether they read pre-normalized or post-normalized streams.

Clarence: Also noticed preview aggregation merges partials by sampling_id + model_alias; if model_alias changes mid-request, we end up double counting unless we dedupe by req_id first. We should prefer req_id when present.

Omar: Let's do an immediate 3-step plan: 1) Becky to patch sku_map with alias synonyms for affected models (quick) 2) Anya to run a scoped recompute of preview aggregates for window 2026-03-27T18:00..2026-03-28T06:00 for tenants flagged in query (zenith-ai + others) 3) Clarence to schedule router-normalizer->aggregator contract test to ensure X-Canonical-Model is available to preview path.

Becky: Will open BILL-3521 and push sku_map changes. Also include a small migration script that maps synonyms to canonical factor.

Anya: My query to find affected tenants: 
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT req_id) as mismatched_reqs
FROM preview.aggregates a
JOIN billing.events b USING (req_id)
WHERE a.window BETWEEN '2026-03-27' AND '2026-03-28'
  AND a.model_alias_raw != b.model_alias_canonical
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY mismatched_reqs DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

Anya: Returns 36 tenants; attaching CSV to BILL-3521. I'll run recompute after Becky patches sku_map.

deploy-bot: Note: canary has router-normalizer v4.0.1; prod rolled out 2026-03-27T22:00Z.

Clarence: Postmortem items: (1) Add dedupe precedence doc: req_id > sampling_id > model_alias for aggregation; (2) Add integration test that simulates alias changes mid-request; (3) Console UI change to separate token_count vs post-token discounts; (4) Add alert preview_vs_final_token_delta_pct > 7% for 15m.

Becky: I'll include (3) in BILL-3521 as a UI ticket.

Anya: OK starting recompute plan, will update BILL-3521 with ETA. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
